activity.title: Excited to share our new publication in IOP Science’s Machine Learning: Earth! Over the past year and a half, Cenlin He and I had the privilege of mentoring Yashnil Mohanty , an exceptionally talented and motivated student from Westmont High School (CA). In this work, Yashnil applied machine learning to examine how wildfire impacts the predictability of snow disappearance in Northern California. We found that ML model accuracy decreases in heavily burned areas due to altered relationships between environmental predictors and snow dynamics. This finding highlights the need to integrate observations with modeling to better constrain simulations and account for wildfire impacts, helping maintain snow model accuracy in post-fire environments. Personally, this has been a highly rewarding experience, mentoring a young scientist who combines technical skill with genuine passion for applying machine learning to Earth science. Congratulations to Yashnil on this lead-author publication 👏

My high school just disqualified me as valedictorian for being unconventional. My journey over the last 4 years had been wildly untraditional; from moving across the world, to finishing all the STEM APs in 2 years of highschool and moving on to college classes. Through the opportunities I was awarded, my graduating GPA was 4.66, 0.10 points over #2 but my story was too unconventional for my school to make me the face of our class. But I have 0 regrets. I would do it all over again. Systems today are designed to discourage non-traditionality, but the path I paved for myself awarded me disproportionate academic learning opportunities, extra time to work on world changing startups, and exposure to entirely new social contexts. If I’ve learnt one lesson throughout highschool it’s to not be afraid to be different because thats what breeds world-changers.

This past Friday marked my last day at NSF NCAR - The National Center for Atmospheric Research . I’m incredibly grateful for the past five years working at a world-class research institution alongside thoughtful and passionate colleagues. The daily conversations around improving the predictability of hydrometeorological systems and the milestones we reached together have been foundational to the scientist I am today. I’m excited to share that today I'm starting a new role as an Associate Research Scientist with University of Maryland and NASA Goddard Space Flight Center . I’m looking forward to bringing my experience and passion for hydrologic modeling and Earth system science to NASA’s Integrated Modeling Virtual Institute (IMVI: https://lnkd.in/ddGdNzwj ), where we will collaborate across disciplines to advance our understanding of the Earth system and deliver actionable insights for society.

I am proud to be part of this high-impact research led by my colleagues at NCAR. Wildfire smoke is an increasing threat to human health, contributing to thousands of deaths per year in the contiguous US. This research found that although structure fires in the wildland-urban interface (WUI) are much smaller in area than vegetated fires, WUI fires are a major source of toxic air pollution, further underscoring the importance of implementing WUI fire mitigation strategies. Thank you Wenfu Tang for leading this important research. https://lnkd.in/gAq5bsgW

We're 4 college students building a startup from our dorm rooms, thousands of miles apart. Yash Seth , Youyi Ding , Shaurya Pedapati , and I. Different cities. Different time zones. One shared vision. Everyday, we are getting on call with our amazing customers. No office. No co-working space. Just laptops, late night calls, and a refusal to wait until "after graduation" to start. Here's what building from our dorms actually looks like: 3am debugging sessions across 2 time zones Shipping features between classes Group calls that start with "wait, what time is it for you?" Progress that compounds because we never stop People ask us why we didn't wait. Because we believe in the mission of helping others. We have more coming soon! #BuildInPublic #CollegeStudents #OnAMission
